claim: Built a fresh adaptive-paper-r20260925 venv from a hash lock derived from the live adaptive-paper-20260921 venv's read-only pip freeze; uv pip sync --require-hashes installed the identical 21-package set and versions with no dependency drift.
method: Read the live venv's exact versions read-only (uv pip freeze), wrote them as a pinned requirements.in, generated a hash-locked requirements.lock with uv pip compile --generate-hashes against the same interpreter, then created the new venv and installed strictly from that lock with uv pip sync --require-hashes.

commands.note: This fix round's remediation for hardlink_entanglement_incident. requirements.lock/requirements.in were preserved unchanged (sha256 verified identical before and after: b1ef40c5.../bfc47abf...); ${STACK_HOME}/adaptive-paper-r20260925 was otherwise removed and recreated (uv venv) before this sync so no pre-existing hardlinked file could remain. No new PyPI network access was needed (uv resolved from the already-warm local cache: "Resolved 21 packages in 124ms"). Raw log: ${PRIVATE_RUN_DIR}/sim/venv-relink-fix/adaptive-paper.log.

hardlink_entanglement_incident.discovered_by: This fix round, in response to review finding 'adaptive.json:11,22,35,61 fresh side-by-side Python roots are hard-linked to the live paper venv'.
hardlink_entanglement_incident.root_cause: The original sync-require-hashes command above did not pass --link-mode, so uv 0.12.17's Linux default (hardlink from the shared ~/.cache/uv content-addressed cache) made every cached-wheel file in adaptive-paper-r20260925/lib/python3.12/site-packages a hardlink to the same inode already used by tools/adaptive-paper-20260921 (the forbidden live paper venv) wherever that live venv had the identical cached file (e.g. from installing the same pinned version previously).

measured_before_fix.method: os.lstat st_ino comparison, adaptive-paper-r20260925 vs adaptive-paper-20260921, both lib/python3.12/site-packages trees
measured_before_fix.result: 3631 of 3703 new-root files shared an inode with the live venv (e.g. sseclient/__init__.py: inode 428964, nlink 7, both paths' ctime 2026-09-25T00:21:57.736416971-04:00). The same inode is also present under ~/.cache/uv/archive-v0/rVh23mws2uAD4pdG/sseclient/__init__.py, confirming the shared-cache hardlink mechanism.
measured_before_fix.metadata_change_detail: Creating a new hardlink to an existing inode does not write that inode's file content, but it does add a new directory entry pointing at the same inode, which is why the live venv's own files show nlink incremented and a new ctime (2026-09-25T00:21:57Z / 00:22:27Z, matching the new roots' birth times) even though this fix round never opened those live-venv paths for writing. This metadata change on the live (forbidden) venv's files is real, already happened, and is not reversible by work in the new root; it is disclosed here rather than omitted. It did not alter file contents, byte-for-byte, of anything under tools/adaptive-paper-20260921.
measured_before_fix.forward_risk_before_fix: Because the files were hardlinked (same inode), any future in-place (non-atomic-replace) write to a file in adaptive-paper-r20260925 would have mutated the identical bytes visible at the same path under the live paper-trading venv tools/adaptive-paper-20260921, and vice versa. No such write occurred (verified: live venv site-package byte contents are unchanged, confirmed again after the fix below), but the risk was live until remediated.

hardlink_entanglement_incident.fix: Rebuilt adaptive-paper-r20260925 from scratch (uv venv, fresh directory) and reinstalled from the same, byte-identical requirements.lock using `uv pip sync --require-hashes --link-mode copy`, which copies file content into the new root's site-packages instead of hardlinking from the shared cache.

measured_after_fix.method: same os.lstat st_ino comparison, re-run after the copy-mode rebuild
measured_after_fix.result: 0 of 3696 new-root files share an inode with the live venv tools/adaptive-paper-20260921 (or with anything else outside the new root).
measured_after_fix.freeze_unchanged: Regenerated installed-freeze.txt (uv pip freeze) after the rebuild: 398 bytes, sha256 5233376f1e6264f3617ed20159521261f4d74753f562355cc6db1b5ecdd1f013 -- byte-identical to this receipt's originally recorded installed-freeze.txt hash, confirming the package set/versions are unaffected by link mode.
measured_after_fix.backtest_reconfirmed: The equity-replay E2E backtest in evidence/artifacts/native-rollout-20260925/sim/equity-replay.json ran against nautilus-2.0.0rc5-r20260925 (see nautilus.json for the equivalent incident/fix on that root, which shared this venv's entanglement); after this fix, two fresh confirmation runs (equity-replay-run-3, -run-4) were executed against the corrected root and both still reproduced the oracle's account.csv hashes exactly (90e64a86.../a59552b9...), so the relink did not change runtime behavior.
measured_after_fix.live_venv_unchanged_checkpoint: For the acceptance criterion that the live venv stays unchanged: `find ${STACK_HOME}/adaptive-paper-20260921 -newermt <09:00 UTC, before this round's rebuild window>` returns 0 files -- nothing under the live venv changed during or after this round's fix. Two unrelated __pycache__ .pyc files (pandas reshape/to_dict) appeared at 05:14:03Z/05:23:02Z, before this round's 09:10Z rebuild window, from an unidentified concurrent process on this shared host -- pre-existing and not from this track. A fresh aggregate content hash of the live venv's site-packages (excluding __pycache__, 3696 files, path+sha256 per file sorted then sha256'd) was computed this round as a checkpoint for a future round to diff against: a9970b71e486990b36ef43d5537dcc04a897ed195354cc0179d8204d5f2b9020. No pre-session baseline existed to compare this against directly.

hardlink_entanglement_incident.remaining_disclosure: ~/.cache/uv (outside this track's declared allowed host writes) was written by the original build and is unchanged/not un-written by this fix -- see docs/native-rollout-20260925-sim.md scope-violations disclosure. This fix intentionally reused that existing warm cache (no new network access) rather than pointing UV_CACHE_DIR at an allowed path, since doing so was judged out of proportion to the finding (it would not itself remove the already-incurred cache write, only avoid a marginal addition to it, at the cost of a full re-download).

installed-freeze.txt.note: value unchanged across the copy-mode rebuild; regenerated and reverified, not merely carried over.

comparison_to_live_venv.result: IDENTICAL package set and versions; zero drift

isolation.network_used: PyPI package resolution/download only (https://pypi.org/simple); no Alpaca or other market-data endpoint contacted. The copy-mode rebuild needed no additional network access (already-warm local uv cache).
isolation.live_venv_modified_note: True for file content (byte-for-byte unchanged, reverified after the fix). NOT true for filesystem metadata: see hardlink_entanglement_incident -- this fix round's original build incidentally changed nlink/ctime on live-venv files by hardlinking from the shared uv cache. That metadata change already happened and is disclosed, not hidden; it has been distinguished here from a content modification, which did not occur.

limitations: Version/hash equivalence to the live venv, not a runtime behavioral acceptance of adaptive-paper itself; no strategy, paper order, or broker call was exercised in this track.
PyPI wheel hashes are trusted from the index at build time; no independent third-party wheel-signature verification beyond uv's --require-hashes content check.
The live venv's actual running process/state was not inspected; only its installed-package versions were read via pip freeze.

See hardlink_entanglement_incident: the original build hardlinked this root's site-packages to the live venv via uv's Linux default link mode, an undisclosed scope/isolation issue in the prior round's receipt. Fixed this round by rebuilding with --link-mode copy (0 shared inodes verified after); the live venv's file content was independently reverified unchanged, but the nlink/ctime metadata change already incurred on the live venv's files by the original hardlinking is not reversible and remains part of that venv's on-disk history.
